user.title: Your solar power sensor
user.description: Pick the sensor(s) that show how much power your panels produce right now (W or kW). With several strings or inverters, pick them all; they are added up. Solar Headroom learns from this sensor's history in Home Assistant.

data_description.pv_power: Power from the panels (DC or inverter PV input), not the house load.

panels.title: Your panels
panels.description: One group of panels that share a direction and tilt. You can add more groups (e.g. east and west roofs) after setup.

data_description.kwp: Total nameplate power of the panels in this group, in kW (e.g. 12 panels × 450 W = 5.4).
data_description.tilt: Angle from horizontal: 0° = flat, 90° = vertical. A guess within 10° is fine.
data_description.azimuth: Compass direction the panels face: 90° = east, 180° = south, 270° = west.

history.title: History found
history.description:
Found {history} of history for your solar sensor.
{signs}

After you finish, Solar Headroom reads it together with weather archives from Open-Meteo and learns your system in the background (a few minutes). Until then the forecast uses physics only.

Only your location rounded to ~10 km and the panel direction and tilt are sent to Open-Meteo. No account, no key.

no_history.title: No history yet
no_history.description:
Home Assistant has no long-term statistics for this sensor yet (it needs `state_class: measurement`). Solar Headroom starts with a physics forecast and learns as data comes in; most systems are learned within a few weeks.

Only your location rounded to ~10 km and the panel direction and tilt are sent to Open-Meteo. No account, no key.

holdback.title: Does your inverter ever hold back solar power?
holdback.description: Inverters throttle the panels when the power has nowhere to go: the battery is full and the house needs little (off-grid), or the grid may not take more (export limit, zero export). Solar Headroom then estimates what the panels could have given instead of learning "low".

data_description.kind: Pick the closest. Grid-tied systems that export freely never hold back.
data_description.export_limit_w: Only for an export limit: the most the grid may take, in W. 0 = zero export.

sensors.title: Battery and grid sensors
sensors.description: These tell Solar Headroom when the panels were giving all they could. Pre-filled from the Energy dashboard where set up. Use power sensors with history (state_class: measurement).

data.battery_power_inverted: Battery power sensor is positive while charging
data.grid_power_inverted: Grid power sensor is positive while exporting

data_description.battery_power: Home Assistant's convention: positive = discharging, negative = charging. Tick the box below if yours is the other way round; the history is checked too.
data_description.battery_soc: Optional but recommended: when the battery is not full, it takes all the panels offer.
data_description.grid_power: Positive = from the grid, negative = to the grid.
data_description.grid_voltage: Optional, off-grid with an occasional grid: tells when the grid is there.
data_description.generator_power: Optional: tells when a generator is running.
data_description.pv_voltage: Optional: a throttled string runs at a higher voltage; Solar Headroom learns your normal band.

error.required: This sensor is needed for the kind of system you picked.

abort.already_configured: These sensors are already set up.

sensor_unavailable.title: Solar Headroom: a sensor gives no reading
sensor_unavailable.description:
{entity} has given no reading for more than an hour of daylight. Until it does, {title} cannot tell whether the panels give all they can, and the live potential falls back to the sky model.

Check the integration that provides the sensor, or pick another sensor in Solar Headroom's options.

forecast_unreachable.title: Solar Headroom: no weather forecast
forecast_unreachable.description: {title} has had no forecast from Open-Meteo for more than 6 hours ({error}). The forecasts and the live estimate use older data until it is back. Check that Home Assistant can reach the internet; nothing else is needed.

no_statistics.title: Solar Headroom: a sensor has no history
no_statistics.description: Home Assistant keeps no long-term statistics for {entity}, so {title} cannot learn from it. Sensors need `state_class: measurement`; most inverter integrations set it. If yours does not, add it with a customization or a template sensor, or pick another sensor in Solar Headroom's options.

confirm.title: Read {entity} the other way round?
confirm.description: Over the last {hours} hours, {entity} moved against the battery's state of charge (or the grid against the solar power) the wrong way: it looks positive where Home Assistant's convention is negative. Solar Headroom will read it the other way round and learn again. You can change this back in the options.
